question_html: What is the primary objective of preparing a Manufacturing Account in manufacturing entities?

options.A: To ascertain the net profit or net loss of the entire business
options.B: To determine manufacturing costs of finished goods for assessing cost effectiveness
options.C: To show the gross profit earned on trading activities
options.D: To exhibit the financial position of assets and liabilities

answer_html: Answer: (B) The objective of preparing a Manufacturing Account is to determine manufacturing costs of finished goods for assessing the cost effectiveness of manufacturing activities[cite: 17].

question_html: How does a Manufacturing Account differ fundamentally from a Trading Account?

options.A: Manufacturing account shows gross profit while trading account shows cost of goods sold.
options.B: Manufacturing account deals with raw materials and work-in-progress, whereas trading account deals with finished goods.
options.C: Manufacturing account is prepared for corporate entities only, while trading account is for sole proprietors.
options.D: Manufacturing account records administrative expenses only.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Manufacturing account deals with raw materials and work-in-progress, while the trading account deals with finished goods only[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following formulas correctly represents 'Raw Material Consumed'?

options.A: Opening Inventory of Raw Materials + Purchases + Closing Inventory of Raw Materials
options.B: Opening Inventory of Raw Materials + Purchases - Closing Inventory of Raw Materials
options.C: Purchases - Opening Inventory of Raw Materials + Closing Inventory of Raw Materials
options.D: Opening Inventory of Raw Materials - Purchases - Closing Inventory of Raw Materials

answer_html: Answer: (B) Raw Material Consumed = Opening inventory of raw materials + Purchases - Closing inventory of raw materials[cite: 17].

question_html: Where are opening and closing inventories of Work-in-Process (WIP) posted in the Manufacturing Account?

options.A: Opening WIP is credited and closing WIP is debited.
options.B: Opening WIP is debited and closing WIP is credited.
options.C: Both opening and closing WIP are debited.
options.D: Both opening and closing WIP are credited.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Opening inventory of Work-in-Process is posted to the debit of the Manufacturing Account and closing inventory of Work-in-Process is posted to the credit[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following is considered a 'Direct Manufacturing Expense'?

options.A: Depreciation of factory building
options.B: Factory lighting and heating
options.C: Royalty based on units produced

answer_html: Answer: (C) Direct manufacturing expenses include royalties for using license or technology if based on units produced, and hire charges of plant and machinery if based on units produced[cite: 17].

question_html: What is 'Overhead' defined as in manufacturing cost accounting?

options.A: Total cost of direct material, direct wages, and direct expenses
options.B: Total cost of indirect material, indirect wages, and indirect expenses
options.C: Total cost of selling and distribution only

answer_html: Answer: (B) Overhead is defined as total cost of indirect material, indirect wages and indirect expenses[cite: 17].

question_html: How should the sale value of a by-product normally be treated in the accounts?

options.A: Credited to the Capital Account
options.B: Credited to the Manufacturing Account to reduce the cost of manufacture of the main product
options.C: Credited to the Sundry Creditors Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) The correct treatment of a by-product is to credit its sale/net realizable value to the Manufacturing Account so as to reduce to that extent the cost of manufacture of the main product[cite: 17].

question_html: In the absence of specific instructions, what assumption must be made for determining the value of closing inventory of finished goods?

options.A: Last-in, first-out (LIFO) basis
options.B: First-in, first-out (FIFO) basis
options.C: Simple average cost basis

answer_html: Answer: (B) In the absence of specific instructions, it must be assumed that sales have been on a first-in, first-out (FIFO) basis, meaning closing inventory consists as far as possible of goods produced during the year[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following is an example of indirect material in manufacturing?

options.A: Raw timber used directly in manufacturing furniture
options.B: Stores consumed for repair and maintenance work, fuel, and lubricating oil
options.C: Primary fabric used in garment production
options.D: Main steel sheets used for car bodies

answer_html: Answer: (B) Indirect materials cannot be linked directly with units produced, such as stores consumed for repair and maintenance work, small tools, fuel, and lubricating oil[cite: 17].

question_html: What does the Trading Account show with respect to quantities of goods?

options.A: Quantities of raw materials and work-in-progress
options.B: Quantities of finished goods manufactured and sold, along with opening and closing inventory
options.C: Quantities of machinery purchased and discarded

answer_html: Answer: (B) The Trading Account will show the quantities of finished goods manufactured and sold and the opening and closing inventory, but not raw materials or work-in-progress[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following is true regarding modern presentation practices for manufacturing entities?

options.A: Every manufacturing entity mandatorily prepares a separate Manufacturing Account as part of final accounts.
options.B: Nowadays, items of manufacturing account are often shown directly in the trading account or statement of profit and loss.
options.C: Manufacturing accounts are prohibited by law.
options.D: Manufacturing accounts replace the Balance Sheet.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Nowadays no manufacturing business entity prepares a manufacturing account as part of its final set of accounts; items are shown either in trading account or in statement of profit and loss[cite: 17].

question_html: What is a by-product?

options.A: A primary product produced with conscious additional expense
options.B: A secondary product produced from the same raw materials incidentally without incurring additional expenses
options.C: Defective main products that are discarded
options.D: Purchased trading goods resold without processing

answer_html: Answer: (B) A by-product is a secondary product produced from the same raw materials used for the main product without incurring any additional expenses from the same production process[cite: 17].

question_html: Why is it useful to maintain quantity columns in a Manufacturing Account?

options.A: To calculate income tax liability
options.B: To ensure that quantities balance and to work out missing quantities such as units sold or manufactured
options.C: To determine the market value of shares

answer_html: Answer: (B) Having quantity columns in the account helps verify that both sides balance and allows calculation of missing quantities[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following is an example of a by-product?

options.A: Sugar produced from sugarcane
options.B: Molasses produced in sugar manufacturing
options.C: Cotton cloth produced from raw cotton

answer_html: Answer: (B) Molasses is a classic example of a by-product in sugar manufacturing[cite: 17].

question_html: What do indirect wages include?

options.A: Direct wages paid to factory production workers per unit
options.B: Wages for maintenance works, holding pay, etc., which cannot be directly linked to units produced
options.C: Commissions paid to sales agents

answer_html: Answer: (B) Indirect wages are those which cannot be directly linked to units produced, such as wages for maintenance works, holding pay, etc.[cite: 17].

question_html: 1,00,000 units were produced in a factory. Per unit material cost was ₹10 and per unit labour cost was ₹5. Royalty was agreed to be paid @ ₹3 per unit to a collaborator. What is the total Manufacturing Cost?
answer_html: Answer: (C) Raw material ($1,00,000 imes 10 = 10,00,000$) + Direct wages ($1,00,000 imes 5 = 5,00,000$) + Direct expenses/royalty ($1,00,000 imes 3 = 3,00,000$) = ₹18,00,000[cite: 17].

question_html: If 5,00,000 units are produced with direct wages contracted at ₹0.80 per unit manufactured and ₹0.40 per unit of closing WIP (12,000 units), what is the total direct wages amount debited?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Direct wages for units produced = $5,00,000 imes 0.80 = 4,00,000$. Wages for closing WIP = $12,000 imes 0.40 = 4,800$. Total = ₹4,04,800[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the effect of an under-statement of closing work-in-progress in an accounting period?

options.A: Overstates cost of goods manufactured
options.B: Understates cost of goods manufactured
options.C: Has no effect on cost of goods manufactured

answer_html: Answer: (A) Since closing WIP is credited in the Manufacturing Account, an under-statement of closing WIP reduces credits, thereby overstating the net cost of goods manufactured[cite: 17].

question_html: In Mr. Shivi's accounts, purchase of machinery worth ₹10,000,000 was omitted (depreciation rate 10%). Wages included ₹50,000 paid to office staff. Direct expenses included ₹24,000 office electricity and ₹20,000 delivery charges to customers. If current transferred balance to Trading Account was ₹17,94,000, what is the revised balance transferred to Trading Account?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Current balance ₹17,94,000 + unrecorded depreciation ₹1,00,000 - office wages ₹50,000 - office electricity ₹24,000 - delivery charges ₹20,000 = ₹18,00,000[cite: 17].

question_html: If opening stock of raw materials is ₹21,000, purchases are ₹85,000, carriage on purchases is ₹1,500 (included in raw material calculation or direct expenses depending on context), and closing stock of raw materials is ₹16,200, what is the raw material consumed?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Raw material consumed = Opening stock ($21,000) + Purchases ($85,000) - Closing stock ($16,200) = ₹89,800[cite: 17].

question_html: In Mr. Pankaj's factory, opening WIP is ₹3,90,000, closing WIP is ₹5,07,000, raw material consumed is ₹11,84,000, direct wages is ₹2,10,000, royalty is ₹1,30,000, and total manufacturing overheads are ₹3,94,000. If by-product selling price is ₹20,000, what is the cost of finished goods transferred to Trading Account?
When preparing a Manufacturing Account, which items are included under Factory Overheads?

options.A: Office salaries and printing stationery
options.B: Repairs & maintenance of plant, factory lighting, factory rent, and factory depreciation
options.C: Sales commission and delivery charges to customers

answer_html: Answer: (B) Factory overheads include indirect expenses and manufacturing overheads such as plant repairs, factory rent, factory lighting, and factory depreciation[cite: 17].

question_html: In Mr. Pandit's trial balance, raw material opening stock is ₹1,50,000, purchases is ₹5,00,000, purchase returns is ₹5,000, carriage inwards is ₹15,000, direct wages is ₹80,000, power is ₹30,000, coal & fuel is ₹15,000, factory rent & rates is ₹20,000, and machinery depreciation is ₹3,000. What is the total cost of manufactured goods transferred to Trading Account?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Summing raw material consumed ($1,50,000 + 4,95,000 - ext{closing stock if any or direct addition}), direct wages, power, coal & fuel, factory rent, carriage inwards, and depreciation equals ₹8,08,000[cite: 17].

question_html: If opening stock of raw materials is ₹1,00,000, creditors opening balance is ₹15,000, bank payments to creditors is ₹22,00,000, creditors closing balance is ₹6,00,000, what is the purchases made during the year?
answer_html: Answer: (C) From Creditors Account: Payments ($22,00,000) + Closing balance ($6,00,000) - Opening balance ($15,00,000) = Purchases of ₹13,00,000 (Wait, check figures: $22,00,000 + 6,00,000 - 15,00,000 = 13,00,000$)[cite: 17].

question_html: Why are lighting and rent expenses apportioned between the factory and the office in manufacturing accounts?

options.A: Because factory expenses belong to the Manufacturing Account while office expenses belong to the Profit and Loss Account.
options.B: Because all expenses must be equally divided regardless of usage.
options.C: To inflate gross profit arbitrarily.
options.D: Because tax authorities require equal splits.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Expenses like rent and lighting must be split between factory (charged to Manufacturing Account) and office (charged to Profit and Loss Account) to reflect correct functional costs[cite: 17].

question_html: In Mr. White's problem, if office premises occupy 1/4th of the total area and total rent is ₹6,000, how much rent is charged to the Manufacturing Account?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Office rent = $1/4 imes 6,000 = 1,500$. Factory rent = $3/4 imes 6,000 = ext{₹}4,500$ charged to Manufacturing Account[cite: 17].

question_html: In Mr. White's problem, if lighting is to be charged as 2/3 to factory and 1/3 to office, and total lighting is ₹1,350, what amount is debited to the Manufacturing Account?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Factory lighting = $2/3 imes 1,350 = ext{₹}900$[cite: 17].

question_html: If plant and machinery has a book value of ₹70,000 and depreciation is to be provided at 10% per annum, what is the depreciation amount charged to the Manufacturing Account?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Depreciation = $10\% ext{ of } 70,000 = ext{₹}7,000$[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the treatment of outstanding wages for March amounting to ₹2,000 in a manufacturing entity's accounts?

options.A: Added to wages in Manufacturing Account and shown as a liability in the Balance Sheet
options.B: Deducted from wages and shown as an asset
options.C: Ignored until paid next year

answer_html: Answer: (A) Outstanding wages are added to wages in the Manufacturing Account and reported as a liability in the Balance Sheet[cite: 17].

question_html: How is 'Sale of Scrap' (arising from manufacturing operations) treated in the Manufacturing Account?

options.A: Credited to the Manufacturing Account
options.B: Debited to the Manufacturing Account
options.C: Shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet

answer_html: Answer: (A) Sale of scrap is credited to the Manufacturing Account to reduce manufacturing costs[cite: 17].

question_html: If opening work-in-progress is ₹9,500, raw material consumed is ₹89,800, wages (including outstanding) is ₹15,000, carriage on purchases is ₹1,500, repairs to plant is ₹1,100, factory rent is ₹4,500, factory lighting is ₹900, plant depreciation is ₹7,000, and closing work-in-progress is ₹7,800, what is the cost of goods manufactured?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total manufacturing cost of goods manufactured transferred to Trading Account is ₹1,19,000[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following statements is FALSE regarding by-products?

options.A: Their production is not consciously undertaken but results incidentally.
options.B: They generally have insignificant value compared to the main product.
options.C: They require a separate manufacturing account with independent raw material allocations.
options.D: They are usually valued at net realizable value.

answer_html: Answer: (C) Statement C is false because by-products do not have separate independent raw material allocations; they result from the same process without additional expenses[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the effect on the Trading Account when cost of goods manufactured is transferred from the Manufacturing Account?

options.A: It is debited to the Trading Account, serving as the cost of production of finished goods.
options.B: It is credited to the Trading Account.
options.C: It is ignored in the Trading Account.
options.D: It is added directly to sales.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Cost of finished goods manufactured is transferred from the Manufacturing Account and debited to the Trading Account[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following functions is served by a Manufacturing Account?

options.A: Providing details of factory cost and facilitating reconciliation of financial books with cost records
options.B: Calculating net profit after tax
options.C: Determining partners' capital ratios
options.D: Assessing cash flow from financing activities

answer_html: Answer: (A) A manufacturing account provides details of factory cost and facilitates reconciliation of financial books with cost records[cite: 17].

question_html: If office furniture is depreciated at 7.5% on an original value of ₹10,000, what is the depreciation amount charged to the Profit and Loss Account?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Office furniture depreciation = $7.5\% ext{ of } 10,000 = ext{₹}750$[cite: 17].

question_html: What are the components that make up 'Prime Cost' in manufacturing accounting?

options.A: Raw Material Consumed + Direct Wages + Direct Expenses
options.B: Indirect Material + Indirect Wages + Overheads
options.C: Opening Stock of Finished Goods + Purchases - Closing Stock

answer_html: Answer: (A) Prime cost comprises Raw Material Consumed + Direct Wages + Direct Expenses[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following is true regarding Guidance Notes issued by ICAI (August 2023 edition) on financial statements for non-corporate entities?

options.A: Standardized formats have been provided to enhance consistency and comparability, though for knowledge only if outside syllabus.
options.B: They make Manufacturing Accounts strictly mandatory for all sole proprietors.
options.C: They prohibit the preparation of Balance Sheets.
options.D: They eliminate the Profit and Loss Account.

answer_html: Answer: (A) The ICAI guidance note provides standardised formats for non-corporate entities to enhance consistency and comparability, given for knowledge/awareness[cite: 17].

question_html: If the opening inventory of raw materials is ₹1,70,000, purchases is ₹8,20,000, and closing inventory of raw materials is ₹1,90,000, what is the raw material consumed?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Raw material consumed = $1,70,000 + 8,20,000 - 1,90,000 = ext{₹}8,00,000$[cite: 17].

question_html: Which of the following items is correctly classified as an indirect manufacturing expense?

options.A: Direct wages paid to machine operators
options.B: Training expenses of factory personnel and factory insurance premium
options.C: Direct royalties on units produced

answer_html: Answer: (B) Indirect expenses include training expenses, depreciation of plant/machinery, and insurance premium for factory shed and plant[cite: 17].

question_html: In Mr. Vimal's factory, hire charges of machine are ₹0.60 per unit manufactured. If 5,000,000 units? Wait, if 5,00,000 units are produced, what are the machine hire charges?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Hire charges = $5,00,000 imes 0.60 = ext{₹}3,00,000$[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the primary distinction between direct and indirect manufacturing expenses?

options.A: Direct expenses can be specifically identified with a particular product or batch, whereas indirect expenses are general overheads incurred for overall manufacturing.
options.B: Direct expenses are paid in cash while indirect expenses are paid by cheque.
options.C: Direct expenses appear in P&L account only, while indirect expenses appear in Trading account.
options.D: There is no difference between them.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Direct expenses are incurred for a specific product or saleable service, whereas indirect expenses cannot be directly linked to units produced[cite: 17].

question_html: If the opening stock of finished goods is ₹15,500, cost of goods transferred from manufacturing account is ₹1,19,000, and closing stock of finished goods is ₹18,100, what is the cost of goods sold before calculating gross profit?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Cost of goods sold = Opening finished goods ($15,500) + Cost of production ($1,19,000) - Closing finished goods ($18,100) = ₹1,16,400[cite: 17].

question_html: How are loose tools or small tools consumed in factory repairs classified?

options.A: Indirect material (manufacturing overhead)
options.B: Direct raw material
options.C: Selling expense

answer_html: Answer: (A) Small tools and stores consumed for repair and maintenance work are classified as indirect materials under manufacturing overhead[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the effect on the Manufacturing Account if raw material returns to suppliers are omitted from being deducted from purchases?

options.A: Raw material consumed and cost of goods manufactured will be overstated.
options.B: Raw material consumed will be understated.
options.C: Gross profit will be unaffected.
options.D: Closing stock of finished goods will increase.

answer_html: Answer: (A) Omitting purchase returns leaves purchases higher, thereby overstating raw material consumed and the cost of goods manufactured[cite: 17].

question_html: When preparing final accounts for a manufacturing entity, where is the provision for doubtful debts usually charged?

options.A: Manufacturing Account
options.B: Profit and Loss Account
options.C: Trading Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Provision for doubtful debts is a general administrative/financial provision charged to the Profit and Loss Account[cite: 17].

question_html: In Mr. Pankaj's factory, raw material purchases is ₹12,10,000, opening raw material is ₹3,02,000, closing raw material is ₹3,10,000, and raw material returned is ₹18,000. What is the net raw material consumed?
Which of the following items would appear in the Manufacturing Account rather than the Trading Account?

options.A: Sales returns
options.B: Work-in-progress closing balance
options.C: Finished goods closing stock

answer_html: Answer: (B) Work-in-progress closing balance appears in the Manufacturing Account, whereas finished goods closing stock appears in the Trading Account[cite: 17].

question_html: What is the effect on net profit if factory depreciation is omitted from being debited to the Manufacturing Account?

options.A: Net profit is overstated
options.B: Net profit is understated
options.C: Net profit is unaffected

answer_html: Answer: (A) Omitting factory depreciation understates manufacturing cost, which overstates cost of goods sold/transferred, or rather understates cost of production initially but overstates profit when goods are sold—actually, lower cost of production reduces trading debit, thus overstating gross profit and net profit[cite: 17].

question_html: How are factory power and fuel expenses treated in the preparation of final accounts?

options.A: Debited to the Manufacturing Account as direct/factory expenses
options.B: Debited to the Profit and Loss Account as administrative expenses
options.C: Credited to the Trading Account

answer_html: Answer: (A) Factory power and fuel expenses are incurred for manufacturing operations and are debited to the Manufacturing Account[cite: 17].

question_html: What role does the Manufacturing Account play in cost accounting reconciliation?

options.A: It provides details of factory cost that facilitate the reconciliation of financial books with cost records.
options.B: It replaces cost sheets entirely.
options.C: It calculates tax payable under GST.

answer_html: Answer: (A) A manufacturing account provides details of factory cost and facilitates the reconciliation of financial books with cost records[cite: 17].
